title: Rawal's Unbeaten Century Powers India to Nine-Wicket Win Over Zimbabwe in Opener
excerpt: Pratika Rawal made 100 not out and Shafali Verma smashed 64 not out from 33 balls as India chased 198 in 27.1 overs in Vadodara, after Shree Charani's 4 for 23 restricted Zimbabwe to 197 in the first ODI of a new three-match series.
body:
• India beat Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the first WODI in Vadodara, chasing 198 in just 27.1 overs to take a 1-0 lead in the new three-match series.
  • Pratika Rawal scored an unbeaten 100 off 96 balls with 15 fours — her third ODI century — and was named Player of the Match.
  • Shree Charani took a career-best 4 for 23 from 10 overs, with three maidens, as Zimbabwe were bowled out for 197 in 49.5 overs despite Beloved Biza's 62.
  • Shafali Verma's unbeaten 64 off 33 balls, with five fours and four sixes, closed out the chase; the second ODI is on Sunday, October 25, at the same venue.

Pratika Rawal struck an unbeaten century and Shree Charani claimed four wickets as India opened a new three-match one-day series against Zimbabwe with a nine-wicket win at the BCA Stadium in Kotambi, Vadodara, on Friday. Chasing 198, India reached 200 for 1 in 27.1 overs, finishing with 22.5 overs to spare in Smriti Mandhana's first ODI match as captain.

The result starts a fresh series — the ODI leg of Zimbabwe's tour of India — rather than extending any earlier contest between the sides, and gives India a 1-0 lead ahead of the second match on Sunday.

Charani strangles Zimbabwe's innings

Zimbabwe, batting first after winning the toss, were bowled out for 197 in 49.5 overs. Beloved Biza held the innings together with 62 off 92 balls, with support from Modester Mupachikwa (25) and a late 29 from Michelle Mavunga, but partnerships never lasted long enough to set a testing total.

Charani was the reason. The spinner returned career-best ODI figures of 4 for 23 from her 10 overs, including three maidens, breaking the innings open through the middle overs, according to CricTracker's match report. Kranti Gaud took 3 for 42, Deepti Sharma 2 for 44, and Shafali Verma chipped in with 1 for 28.

"Pratika Rawal was the standout performer with the bat for the Indian side. The opener scored a magnificent unbeaten century off 96 balls, hitting 15 fours in her knock."

— CricTracker match report

Rawal anchors, Shafali detonates

India's chase, reported in detail by the Times of India, was controlled from the first over. Rawal and Mandhana put on 94 for the first wicket before the captain fell for 32 off 34 balls, caught by Biza off Olinda Chare — Zimbabwe's only wicket of the innings.

Shafali Verma then turned a comfortable chase into a rout. She made 64 not out from 33 balls, with five fours and four sixes at a strike rate of 193.94, sharing an unbeaten 106-run second-wicket stand with Rawal off just 70 balls and finishing the match with a boundary. Rawal's hundred, her third in ODIs, came off 96 balls and earned her the Player of the Match award.

What it means for the series

For India, the match answered two questions at once: Rawal, returning to the side, immediately re-established herself as the anchor at the top of the order, and Charani's control gives Mandhana a genuine wicket-taking spin option in the middle overs. Zimbabwe's one clear positive was Biza, whose 62 showed the technique to build an innings — but no teammate passed 29, and a sub-200 total was never likely to trouble this Indian batting line-up on a good surface.

The teams meet again at the same venue on Sunday, October 25, for the second ODI, with the third match scheduled for Wednesday, October 28. Zimbabwe need a win on Sunday to keep the series alive; India can seal it with a match to spare.
